verdicts.label: 2A
verdicts.note: Verified on the tender API: 150 genomes, budget NT$2.25M, base price NT$1.82M, awarded 29 Oct 2024 to 台基盟 at NT$1.47M (NT$9,800 each). The rival 基龍米克斯 bid NT$1,899,750 and was not the lowest bid. Two caveats: (1) the hospital comparison is across periods (the NHRI award is Oct 2024, the hospital awards are 2025–26) and across scope (the hospital awards include clinical work and blood draw); (2) the price fight is between two Illumina-based service vendors, so the discount comes out of vendor margin first. The link to NHRI ending its S4 purchases is an inference from F712.

verdicts.label: 2B
verdicts.note: Verified for 115B005-2: the tender is a chicken (紅羽土雞) NGS service. Budget NT$2.6M, base NT$2.5M, one bidder, KIMFOREST at NT$2,499,500. The qualification clause requiring purchase proof for an X Plus located in Taiwan is quoted as stated. The 2025 award (NT$1,595,880, 28% under a NT$2.22M base, three bidders) was not re-checked. It is a small agricultural research buyer, so this is lock-in evidence, not a volume datapoint.

derived.label: 1B
derived.claim: Taiwan's NHRI bought outsourced 30x genomes at about US$305 all-in in Oct 2024. After library prep and analysis, that leaves the Illumina-based vendor only about $1.0–2.0/Gb for reagents and margin, at or below the Open Offer top-tier net of $1.76/Gb.
derived.detail: NT$1.47M / 150 = NT$9,800 per genome, or about US$305 at ~32 NT$/US$ (Oct 2024). Using TCAG's split (PCR-free prep ~US$100 and QC/analysis ~US$100–130; D043), about $75–205 remains for ~100 Gb, which is ~$0.75–2.0/Gb including the vendor's margin. That compares with ~$2.0/Gb list for the 25B-300, $1.76/Gb Open Offer top tier (D051) and $2.55/Gb Novogene lanes. Large Taiwanese service vendors therefore appear to buy X reagents at least near the best published net prices, which fits steep large-account discounts.

derived.label: 1B
derived.claim: Outsourced WGS prices in Taiwan fell in one step from NT$24,000 (2023) to NT$9,800–12,800 (2024–25), then held flat at NT$12,800 across 2025–26 awards. That looks like a one-time NovaSeq X conversion step, not accelerating deflation.
derived.detail: Taipei VGH paid NT$24,000 per WGS in the Jul 2023 contract and NT$12,800 in Feb 2025 (−47%; D068). NHRI paid NT$9,800 in Oct 2024. Kaohsiung VGH paid exactly NT$12,800 in Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 (F744), so there was no further decline over about 12 months. The same pattern shows up in Taipei VGH's flat NT$201,000 P4 price in 2025–26 (F713).
derived.source_name: Taiwan e-Procurement (Taipei VGH, Kaohsiung VGH, NHRI)
derived.why_new: Joins the 2023 price, the 2024 research price and the 2025–26 hospital prices into a time series showing a step and then a plateau.

derived.label: 2B
derived.claim: In Taiwanese research sequencing tenders, multi-bidder awards came in 19–28% below base price, while single-bidder awards with Illumina-only qualification clauses landed at 0–0.02% below base. Illumina spec clauses largely remove the research price fight.
derived.detail: Multi-bidder awards: NHRI WGS NT$1.47M vs NT$1.82M base (−19%, 2 bidders, Oct 2024) and the Livestock Research Institute 2025 award NT$1,595,880 vs NT$2.22M base (−28%, 3 bidders). Single-bidder awards with Illumina clauses: Livestock Research Institute 2026 NT$2,499,500 vs NT$2.5M (−0.02%, requires an X Plus in Taiwan) and TMU WGS NT$3,057,600 = base (requires two or more Illumina high-throughput sequencers, re-tendered after failing). Research buyers get deep discounts only where vendors compete, and that competition is among Illumina-based vendors.
